guide.title: Berlin, Connecticut: Tinware Peddlers and the Oldest Civil War Monument
guide.intro: European settlement traces to 1659, when Sergeant Richard Beckley bought 300 acres from Chief Tarramuggus in what was then the Great Swamp Society; the General Assembly incorporated the town as Berlin in 1785, and New Britain split off from it in 1850. Around 1740, Irish immigrant brothers Edward and William Pattison set up the first tinware business in the American colonies here, launching the door-to-door "Yankee Peddler" trade still pictured on the town seal. Berlin native Emma Hart Willard, a pioneer of women's higher education, was born in 1787 and opened the Troy Female Seminary in 1821. On March 9, 1799, Simeon North of Berlin received the U.S. government's first pistol contract; he went on to pioneer interchangeable-parts manufacturing. The geographic center of Connecticut lies within Berlin, which today comprises Berlin Center, Kensington and East Berlin.

sections.heading: The oldest Civil War monument in the country
sections.body: The Kensington Soldiers Monument, dedicated July 28, 1863 — less than a month after Gettysburg — is recognized as the country's oldest permanent Civil War monument. It was designed by Kensington resident Nelson Augustus Moore, a Hudson River School-associated landscape artist, from brown Portland sandstone moved by a sledge drawn by 14 oxen to a Bacon quarry in East Berlin for finishing, and it still stands on the grounds of the Kensington Congregational Church. Ragged Mountain, whose traprock cliffs straddle Berlin and Southington, is one of Connecticut's premier rock-climbing destinations, with the 51-mile Metacomet Trail running its ridge; the main trailhead is on West Lane off Route 71A in Berlin, about 2.75 miles south of downtown New Britain.

sections.heading: Getting there
sections.body: Berlin sits at the crossroads of central Connecticut: Route 9 has a grade-separated interchange with the Berlin Turnpike (US 5/Route 15), a 12.17-mile commercial arterial running from Meriden to the Wethersfield-Hartford line; Route 372 also connects to the Turnpike, and Interstate 91 exit 20 is the nearest access for the Lamentation Mountain side of town; Ragged Mountain's trailhead is reached separately via Route 71A. Unusually for a town this size, Berlin has its own real rail stop: Berlin station, 51 Depot Road, is one of nine CTrail Hartford Line stations between New Haven Union Station and Springfield Union Station, also served by Amtrak Northeast Regional and Valley Flyer trains, with 235 free parking spaces. Metro-North's New Haven Line and Shore Line East do not serve Berlin; connections to those systems are made at New Haven Union Station.

faq.question: How do I get to Berlin?
faq.answer: By car via Route 9, Interstate 91, or the Berlin Turnpike (US 5/Route 15) — or by train: Berlin station, 51 Depot Road, is a stop on the CTrail Hartford Line, also served by Amtrak Northeast Regional and Valley Flyer trains.

faq.question: Is there a train to Berlin?
faq.answer: Yes. Berlin station is one of nine Hartford Line stations between New Haven Union Station and Springfield Union Station, with 235 free parking spaces, a ticket vending machine and bike racks. Metro-North and Shore Line East do not reach Berlin; connect at New Haven Union Station.

faq.question: What is the Kensington Soldiers Monument?
faq.answer: A brown sandstone Civil War monument dedicated July 28, 1863, recognized as the country's oldest permanent Civil War monument. It stands on the grounds of the Kensington Congregational Church.

faq.question: Is there hiking in Berlin?
faq.answer: Yes — Ragged Mountain Memorial Preserve, straddling Berlin and Southington, has traprock cliffs and the blue-blazed Metacomet Trail; the main trailhead is on West Lane off Route 71A in Berlin.

faq.question: Is there a hotel in Berlin?
faq.answer: Yes — Days Inn by Wyndham Berlin Meriden on the Berlin Turnpike is a verified operating property. Call ahead to confirm rates and availability.

places.name: Kensington Soldiers Monument
places.address: Kensington Congregational Church grounds, Kensington section of Berlin, CT 06037
places.summary: Dedicated July 28, 1863 and recognized as the country's oldest permanent Civil War monument, commemorating six fallen Kensington residents. Designed by Hudson River School-associated artist Nelson Augustus Moore from brown Portland sandstone; owned and maintained by the Kensington Congregational Church.

places.name: Ragged Mountain Memorial Preserve
places.address: Main trailhead on West Lane, off Route 71A, Berlin, CT 06037
places.summary: Traprock cliffs from 20 to 60 feet, among Connecticut's premier rock-climbing terrain, including the well-known "Running Man" face. The 51-mile Metacomet Trail runs the length of the ridge; the Red Dot Trail is the easiest route to the summit. Held under a conservation restriction with the Berlin Land Trust.

places.name: Timberlin Golf Club
places.summary: An 18-hole municipal course designed by Al Zikorus and built in 1970, playing to par 72 at 6,733 yards from the championship tees. The on-site Par For The Course restaurant serves golfers and the public; junior, women's, senior and men's club programs run through the season. Phone (860) 828-7987.

places.name: Kensington Pizza
places.summary: A family-run pizzeria established in 1974, with Italian-style pizza alongside pasta, calzones, wings, subs and burgers. Open daily 11 a.m.-9 p.m., with online ordering for carryout and delivery. Phone (860) 828-0949.

places.name: SoulFully Vegan
places.summary: A plant-based kitchen that grew from a food truck into a sit-down restaurant, known for its burgers and boldly spiced dishes drawing on diverse culinary traditions. Open Tue-Thu 11 a.m.-8 p.m., Fri-Sat 11 a.m.-10 p.m., closed Sun-Mon.

places.name: East Tokyo Asian Restaurant
places.summary: A neighborhood Japanese and Asian restaurant on the Farmington Avenue corridor, with active takeout and online ordering. Phone (860) 828-8808.

places.name: Bill's Farmington Ave Pizza
places.summary: An independent Berlin pizzeria offering pickup and curbside pickup. Open daily 11:00 a.m.-9:30 p.m. Phone (860) 979-6282.

places.name: Days Inn by Wyndham Berlin Meriden
places.summary: A newly renovated Berlin Turnpike hotel with live online booking. Phone (860) 438-6178.

places.name: Berlin Station
places.summary: One of nine CTrail Hartford Line stations between New Haven and Springfield, also served by Amtrak Northeast Regional and Valley Flyer trains. The historic 1900 depot burned in a December 2016 fire; the rebuilt station opened June 16, 2018 alongside the launch of Hartford Line service. 235 free parking spaces, ticket vending machine and bike racks.
